purpose: Evaluate the whole power chain, from conversion to the rack and its supporting services.
caption: Conceptual scope: MV AC conversion, LVDC distribution, rack conversion and supporting services. Individual stages depend on the selected architecture.

purpose: The adoption stages move the DC boundary upstream; they do not remove every AC or DC/DC stage.
caption: Three adoption boundaries: racks, an IT module, and broader facility distribution. These are alternatives to evaluate, not a compulsory progression.

purpose: Locate voltage conversion, regulation and galvanic isolation separately.
caption: Isolation location is a design choice. Verify the actual converter topology and the electrical boundary it provides.

purpose: Availability needs both adequate capacity and a viable route.
caption: Compare distinct source and feeder failures, then an explicitly changed feeder arrangement. Usable paths and adequate capacity are separate conditions; shared dependencies remain.
motion_plan: Where redundancy actually works; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.

purpose: Read the band together with its allowed behavior and duration.
caption: B1–B7 classify blackout, operating, protective and prohibited regions. This conceptual ladder does not assign universal numerical thresholds or durations.

purpose: Compatibility includes delivered voltage, power and ride-through duration.
caption: Source and load terminals are different boundaries. The paper’s p. 76 resistive-drop example is followed by separate qualitative demand and voltage-time comparisons.
motion_plan: What voltage reaches the rack?; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.

purpose: Midpoint M may carry normal load current. Protective earth PE has a different role.
caption: Conceptual bipolar load connections. M participates in the intended load circuit when distributed; PE remains a separate protective function.

purpose: Midpoint current follows the imbalance between pole loads.
caption: Normalized conventional currents in a declared bipolar load circuit. Midpoint current follows the signed load difference; PE remains separate from normal load return.
motion_plan: Follow the midpoint current; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.

purpose: An isolation barrier, an earth reference and an insulation monitor perform different functions.
caption: Separate the isolation boundary from the earth-reference and monitoring functions. The sketch identifies responsibilities without prescribing a connection scheme.

purpose: A DC fault can draw energy from source-side capacitors, converters and connected loads.
caption: Three possible contributions to a DC fault. The relative magnitude and timing depend on the actual network, stored energy and converter response.

purpose: Coordinate selectivity with healthy-load hold-up and voltage tolerance.
caption: Illustrative comparison of fault contributions, branch interruption and healthy-load tolerance. Both cases clear the fault; only Case A stays within the assumed tolerance.
motion_plan: One fault, two load outcomes; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.

purpose: A reported OFF state does not prove that every hazardous energy path has been removed.
caption: Commanded state, reported state and verified electrical condition are distinct. Stored energy and alternate sources must be included in the isolation concept.

purpose: Utility-interface performance and internal DC continuity are different requirements.
caption: One event can produce different outcomes at the utility connection and inside the DC system. Evaluate each boundary against its own requirements.

purpose: Match storage placement, power, energy and recharge to the required support.
caption: An illustrative load step connects overlapping support, accumulated energy and recharge demand. Rack buffering does not supply the separately drawn CDU branch.
motion_plan: Who supplies the load step?; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.

purpose: A suitable distribution path needs current, thermal, voltage-drop and DC-duty evidence.
caption: The source-to-load path includes cable drop, thermal limits, connector duty and switching behavior. Each interface needs ratings for the actual DC application.

purpose: The rack entry choice assigns conversion, distribution and control responsibilities.
caption: Three rack interface approaches adapted from the paper’s Figure 9.1. Locate downstream conversion and protection responsibilities in each actual implementation.

purpose: Distinguish initial connection, bulk charging and load enable.
caption: Three distinct events: initial connection, controlled bulk charging and load application. Functional redraw based on paper Figures 9.6–9.10; event scales and levels are illustrative.
motion_plan: Inside a controlled rack connection; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.

purpose: Rack buffering handles local excursions; facility backup has a different boundary and energy requirement.
caption: Local buffering and facility support have different boundaries. Coordinate response, recharge, monitoring and protection across both.

purpose: The fastest protective actions must remain local when supervisory communication is unavailable.
caption: Indicative hierarchy from L0 local action to L4 oversight. Response requirements are system-specific; essential fast protection remains autonomous.

purpose: Every operating transition needs conditions, ownership and evidence.
caption: A branching sequence separates permitted admission, blocked cooling readiness, recovery, fault lockout and maintenance verification. Thresholds and timing remain equipment- and site-specific.
motion_plan: Permission to energize; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.

purpose: A reclose decision needs a known fault response and valid recovery conditions.
caption: Fault recovery and maintenance verification need explicit ownership and evidence. A controller status is one input to the process, not a substitute for every required check.

purpose: Trace the complete high-frequency return path.
caption: Complete differential and common mode loops in one conceptual layout. Filtering changes high-frequency current routes; earth is not an ideal sink or a universal zero-impedance reference.
motion_plan: Noise always has a return path; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.

purpose: A filter’s earth-related capacitance also affects monitoring and fault behavior.
caption: Filters, cables and earth-reference functions share current paths. Review noise mitigation together with insulation monitoring and the selected earthing arrangement.

purpose: Individually functional converters can interact when connected to a shared bus.
caption: A regulated load may demand more current as voltage falls. Stability depends on the combined source, load, cable, filter and control behavior.

purpose: System, product, installation and utility requirements govern different boundaries.
caption: Different boundaries require different evidence and reviewers. A result at one boundary does not automatically settle the others.

purpose: A review conclusion must stay within the scope of its evidence.
caption: A fictional proposal: compare each claim with its required evidence and the limits of what that evidence establishes.

purpose: Fictional scenario: two sources share a bus; each illustrated rack branch has one feeder.
caption: Fictional review case, not an engineered design. The healthy-branch continuity claim is conditional; the affected rack has no demonstrated alternate feeder.

purpose: Review selectivity, hold-up, cooling and recovery against the evidence.
caption: Apply the declared single-feeder scenario across protection, rack tolerance, storage, cooling and recovery. Distinguish topology, assumptions and missing service evidence.
motion_plan: Follow the fault through the whole system; five narration-timed scenes, one finite pass.
